title: Orchard mock runtime fallback on macOS: prove the operations without a model
purpose: Fallback lane for a machine that cannot run the pinned real small model. Every operation is real: pull, serve, bind, request, list, stop, recover. Every output is a labeled course fixture. This recipe proves operations, never model behavior; quality, memory, context, and throughput claims require the real lane or its recorded read-along.
hardware_class: fallback fixture; no model hardware claim
runtime: Code With Vibes Orchard Mock Runtime
prerequisites: Python 3.9 or newer on the PATH; confirm with step 1
A copy of the orchard-mock-runtime folder; no network access is needed at any step

steps.purpose: Confirm the only prerequisite: standard-library Python.
steps.expected_output: Python 3.9 or newer prints its version string.
steps.stop: Nothing to stop; the command exits immediately.
common_errors: command not found: install Python 3 from python.org, then open a new terminal window.

steps.purpose: Create and verify the mock artifact. This is the pull drill: progress, checksum, manifest, and lock handling with zero network.
steps.expected_output: Eleven MOCK lines, opening with MOCK NOTICE no model weights will be downloaded, reporting sha256=f5277bd414643c90b16022e3a388513bf54b6f7377c49461789f7be108c9cc45, and ending with MOCK complete this artifact proves pull and verification mechanics only. A second run verifies the checksum and reports MOCK cached instead.
steps.stop: Ctrl+C is safe at any point; rerunning the pull verifies or recreates the artifact.
common_errors: MOCK ERROR mock_unknown_model, exit 2: use a model name from catalog.json.
MOCK ERROR mock_stale_artifact_lock, exit 5: rerun with --recover-stale-lock exactly as the error's recover line says.

steps.purpose: Start the mock server on loopback and watch the load, memory, and timing lines, each labeled as scenario metadata.
steps.expected_output: The startup transcript ends with MOCK ready base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8133/v1, then MOCK does not think; it proves the operations, and the terminal stays attached to the run.
steps.stop: Ctrl+C in this terminal, or the stop command in step 6 from another terminal. Both produce the same clean state transition.
steps.undo: Stopping the run is the undo; generated state stays under .orchard-runtime until step 7 deletes it.
common_errors: MOCK ERROR mock_port_in_use, exit 2: another listener owns 8133; add --port with a free port and use that port in steps 4 and 5.
MOCK ERROR mock_model_not_pulled, exit 2: run step 2 first; the error prints the exact command.

steps.purpose: Prove the HTTP surface answers before any application code exists. Run this in a SECOND terminal.
steps.expected_output: A JSON object with object list, a data array containing orchard-3b-instruct owned by course-mock, and mock true.
steps.stop: Nothing to stop; the request returns immediately.
steps.undo: Nothing to undo; a GET changes no state.
common_errors: URLError Connection refused: the serve terminal is not ready yet or was stopped; check step 3's terminal.

steps.purpose: Inspect running mock state the way an operator would.
steps.expected_output: A three-line listing: the column header, one ready row for local-001 on 127.0.0.1:8133 with reported 3584, and the line MOCK rows=1 memory is scenario metadata, not measured process memory.
steps.stop: Nothing to stop; ps exits immediately.
steps.undo: Nothing to undo; ps reads state, never writes it.
common_errors: STATUS shows stale: the serve process died without a clean stop; run the stop command in step 6 to recover the state file safely.

steps.purpose: Stop the run from outside, the way a service gets stopped in practice.
steps.expected_output: MOCK stop requested run_id=local-001, then MOCK stopped run_id=local-001 status=clean. The serve terminal adds MOCK shutdown reason=stop-command run_id=local-001 and exits with code 0.
steps.stop: This IS the stop; it exits when the run confirms.
steps.undo: Start the run again with step 3; state and artifact survive a stop.
common_errors: MOCK ERROR mock_run_not_found, exit 3: the run id does not match; check ps for the ids that exist.

steps.purpose: Leave the machine exactly as it started.
steps.expected_output: No output; the generated state directory is gone and nothing else was touched.
steps.stop: Nothing to stop; the command exits immediately.
steps.undo: Run step 2 again; the fixture recreates identically, checksum and all.

health_check: python3 orchard_runtime.py ps --state-dir .orchard-runtime lists run local-001 as ready on 127.0.0.1:8133
expected_result: The run reaches MOCK ready, the test request returns the mock model list, and stop exits cleanly with code 0. Every generated content line begins [COURSE MOCK, NOT MODEL OUTPUT], and no step touches the network.
privacy_notes: No network: the pull creates a local fixture and every request stays on this machine.
No credentials: the runtime reads no API key and the connection profile's secret_env is null.
Loopback by default: the server binds 127.0.0.1 unless you explicitly run the exposure drill.

The exposure drill (--bind 0.0.0.0) really listens on every interface and warns first; use fixture data only, inspect the bind, then stop the run. Firewall policy decides who else can reach an exposed port.
known_failures: Planted OOM: --reported-memory-mib above --memory-limit-mib exits 4 without allocating anything.
Port conflict: a second serve on the same address exits 2 with mock_port_in_use.
Slow load: --load-delay-ms holds STATUS at loading; a stop request during load still works.
Stale artifact lock: scripts/plant_failure.py plants one; pull exits 5 until rerun with --recover-stale-lock.
